context: Collapsible hierarchical tree of biological taxonomy (Life → Domain → Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family) with search, expand/collapse controls, and a categorical color legend by rank
first_impression: A structurally honest tree visualization where encoding is purely categorical and positional — no quantitative scales means most classic deception vectors simply do not apply.
what_works: Color encodes taxonomic rank categorically with a clear legend; descendant count labels (+N) are computed correctly via a recursive function and shown as plain text rather than size-encoded glyphs, avoiding any area-scaling lie factor.
what_doesnt: Key functions use `d.data.name + d.depth` as identity, which would cause DOM corruption if two siblings shared a name — a real-data robustness gap; `nodeSize([22, 220])` is hardcoded rather than derived from data extent, so the layout would not adapt correctly under the scaling metamorphic transform.
